record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: For the R-stadium, the boundary of the R-neighborhood of a segment, determine all maximal distance minimizers for radius r in the range r<R<5r. Also determine the sharp thresholds for existence of non-horseshoe minimizers and for guaranteed horseshoe minimizers of closed curves with prescribed minimal radius of curvature.

evidence.quote: Question 1.2. What is the set of maximal distance minimizers for R-stadium (which is the boundary of R-neighborhood of a segment)? Open for r < R < 5r.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a nonempty compact set and $r>0$. A connected closed set $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is called a maximal distance minimizer for $M$ with radius $r$ if it minimizes the one-dimensional Hausdorff length $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma)$ among all connected closed sets $\Sigma'\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying $\max_{x\in M}\mathrm{dist}(x,\Sigma')\le r$.

For $R>0$, the $R$-stadium is the set $M=\partial(N_R([AB]))$, the boundary of the closed $R$-neighborhood of a line segment $[AB]\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ of positive length. A horseshoe is a planar set consisting of an arc of a circle of radius $R-r$ together with two segments of tangent lines to that arc.

Tasks:
(a) For every $r$ with $r<R<5r$, describe all maximal distance minimizers for the $R$-stadium with radius $r$.
(b) Determine the sharp threshold $R_1(r)$ such that for all $R\le R_1(r)$ there exists a maximal distance minimizer (for the $R$-stadium with radius $r$) that is not a horseshoe, and the sharp threshold $R_2(r)$ such that for all $R\ge R_2(r)$ every maximal distance minimizer is a horseshoe. More generally, for closed convex curves $M\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with prescribed minimal radius of curvature, determine the sharp thresholds guaranteeing existence of non-horseshoe minimizers and, respectively, guaranteed horseshoe-only minimizers.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed among current open questions. For the $R$-stadium it is known that every minimizer is a horseshoe when $R>5r$, while for $R<1.75r$ the minimizer is not a horseshoe; the regime $r<R<5r$ remains open. The related horseshoe conjecture for a circle is confirmed only for $R>4.98r$ (Cherkashin–Teplitskaya and related works).

status_evidence.claim: The R-stadium minimizer problem is open in the range r<R<5r.

status_evidence.title: On the horseshoe conjecture for maximal distance minimizers
status_evidence.snippet: Miranda, Paolini and Stepanov conjectured that any minimizer for a circle of radius R>r is a horseshoe; confirmed for sufficiently large R/r.
status_evidence.claim: The horseshoe conjecture is only partially established, with sharp thresholds still unknown.
